Before you mesh or solve, run the layout check, `simulation_drc`, on the plan
you will give the simulation. It builds the 3D model that simulation would
build, looks for anything too small for the mesher, and says where it is and
who fixes it. It meshes and solves nothing: for the square pad below it takes
under a second, so you can run it whenever the layout changes.

## The recipe {#recipe}

Build the plan, call the check of the simulation you will run, and print the
report. This is the plan of [First simulation](../start/first-simulation.qmd),
built by a function so that the gap between pad and ground can change:

```python
import gdsfactory as gf
import orcapen_sc_pdk
from orcapen_sc_pdk import get_material_records
from orcapen_sc_pdk.tech import get_single_die_layer_stack
from scgsim.geometry import GeometryPlan
from scgsim.palace import ElectrostaticSim

orcapen_sc_pdk.activate()


def pad_plan(gap_um):
    """The square pad of First simulation, with the gap to the ground in µm."""
    component = gf.get_component(
        "square_pad_capacitor", pad_side_um=200.0, gap_um=gap_um, die_side_um=1000.0
    )
    plan = GeometryPlan(
        component=component,
        root_id="chip",
        layer_stack=get_single_die_layer_stack(),
        material_records=get_material_records(),
        coupon_padding_um=0.0,
    )
    plan.set_nets({"pad": ("chip/PAD",), "ground": ("chip/GROUND",)})
    plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=(0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
    return plan


report = ElectrostaticSim.simulation_drc(pad_plan(gap_um=20.0))
print(report.render_text())
```

The 20 µm gap passes:

```text
geometry stage: passed
meshing stage: passed (0 refusing, 0 warning)
```

The check runs in two stages. The **geometry stage** builds the model, as the
simulation's `mesh()` would; a layout that cannot be built stops here with the
error the build raises, such as two Nets that touch. The **meshing stage**
measures every edge and face of the built model and lists those too small for
the mesher. [How a plan is built](prepare-a-layout.qmd) explains what the plan
holds.

## Read a refused report {#read-a-refused-report}

Draw the same pad with a 5 nm gap. The model still builds, but a 5 nm slit is
far too narrow to fill with usable tetrahedra, so the meshing stage refuses it
and raises `SimulationDrcError`, whose `report` holds every finding:

```python
from scgsim.palace import SimulationDrcError

try:
    ElectrostaticSim.simulation_drc(pad_plan(gap_um=0.005))
except SimulationDrcError as error:
    print(error.report.render_text())
```

```text
geometry stage: passed
meshing stage: refused (2 refusing, 2 warning)
  meshing stage, refuse B: face width 2A/P 0.00498753 um (4.99 grid steps) < 10 grid steps at (100.0025, 0.0000, 0.0000) um, f:78b2f2949a9aec64 in PORT::PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000 on layer D0_TOP_M1; from PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge2, PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge6, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge2, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge1; owner layout. A face this narrow forces flat elements along its whole length; refining it does not make them better shaped. Fix: widen or remove the sliver between these polygons.
  meshing stage, refuse B: face width 2A/P 0.00499997 um (5 grid steps) < 10 grid steps at (0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000) um, f:cd87e808586a1f62 in SA::D0_SUBSTRATE|VACUUM_REGION__interface on layer D0_TOP_M1; from PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge2, PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge6, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge0, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge1, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge3, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge4, chip/GROUND/polygon0/ring1/edge5, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge0, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge2, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge3, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge4, chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge5; owner layout. A face this narrow forces flat elements along its whole length; refining it does not make them better shaped. Fix: widen or remove the sliver between these polygons.
  meshing stage, warn C: edge length 0.005 um (5 grid steps) < 25 grid steps at (100.0025, -1.0000, 0.0000) um, e:37415fdfc71dddc3 in PORT::PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000, SA::D0_SUBSTRATE|VACUUM_REGION__interface on layer D0_TOP_M1; from PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge6; owner layout. An edge this short needs elements of its own length around it, which costs repair rounds and elements. Fix: join the short outline edge into its neighbours.
  meshing stage, warn C: edge length 0.005 um (5 grid steps) < 25 grid steps at (100.0025, 1.0000, 0.0000) um, e:78e284ff15d36d88 in PORT::PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000, SA::D0_SUBSTRATE|VACUUM_REGION__interface on layer D0_TOP_M1; from PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000/polygon0/ring0/edge2; owner layout. An edge this short needs elements of its own length around it, which costs repair rounds and elements. Fix: join the short outline edge into its neighbours.
```

Each finding is one line. The first one reads:

| Part of the line | What it says |
|---|---|
| `refuse B` | It stops the layout (`warn` does not), and it is class B: a face too narrow. |
| `face width 2A/P 0.00498753 um (4.99 grid steps) < 10 grid steps` | Its size, against the limit. On this layout's 1 nm grid, 10 grid steps are 0.01 µm. |
| `at (100.0025, 0.0000, 0.0000) um` | Where it is, in layout coordinates: x = 100.0025 µm is the middle of the gap beside the pad's east edge at x = 100 µm. |
| `in PORT::PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000` | The object in the model: the junction sheet the PDK draws across the gap. |
| `on layer D0_TOP_M1` | The layer of the drawn objects it comes from. |
| `from chip/PAD/polygon0/ring0/edge1, ...` | The drawn edges that bound it. |
| `owner layout` | Who acts: the layout is drawn this way. |
| `Fix: widen or remove the sliver between these polygons.` | What to change. |

The second finding is the substrate surface in the same 5 nm ring around the
pad; the two warnings are the 5 nm ends of the junction sheet. Widen the gap
and both refusals go.

The owner says who acts on a finding:

| Owner | Who acts |
|---|---|
| `layout` | You: the fine feature is drawn in the layout. SCGSim reports it and never repairs it. |
| `erosion` | You: Surface-EPR bands from two edges meet, as on a conductor barely wider than twice its margin. Change the margins or the conductor's width. |
| `sgb` | SCGSim: the model builder made a fine feature the layout does not have. Report it to SCGSim with the finding; the layout needs no change. |

A geometry-stage refusal is the build's own error, such as `ContactError` for
two Nets that touch, with its place in µm. [When something
fails](../reference/supported-scope.qmd#when-something-fails) gives the owner
and the next step for each error. If a message does not match the layout you
drew, report it to SCGSim.

### Surface-EPR margins too narrow {#margins-too-narrow}

A Surface-EPR request whose band is narrower than 10 grid steps is refused
before anything is built. Ask for a 5 nm margin on the same pad:

```python
from orcapen_sc_pdk import (
    get_interface_preset_records,
    validate_interface_preset_records,
)

presets = validate_interface_preset_records(get_interface_preset_records())
film = presets["LiteratureCentral_MA"]
plan = pad_plan(gap_um=20.0)
plan.set_surface_epr(
    {
        "MA": {
            "thickness": film["thickness"],
            "permittivity": film["permittivity"],
            "loss_tangent": film["loss_tangent"],
            "inset_margins_um": (0.005,),
        }
    }
)
try:
    ElectrostaticSim.simulation_drc(plan)
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)
```

```text
Surface EPR bands narrower than the meshing stage's face-width limit of 10 grid steps (0.01 um): MA inset_margins_um band=0 (0 to 0.005 um) is 0.005 um (5 grid steps) wide. A band this narrow is a face the mesher cannot use. Widen the inset margins given to plan.set_surface_epr so that every band is at least 10 grid steps wide. Change it in the call to GeometryPlan.set_surface_epr.
```

With `(0.5, 1.0)` µm, as in [Prepare a layout](prepare-a-layout.qmd#surface-epr),
the same pad passes both stages with no warning.

## Which check to run {#which-check-to-run}

Each simulation class checks the model it builds itself, so run the check of
every simulation the cell is meant for:

| The cell is meant for | The call |
|---|---|
| Palace Eigenmode | `scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, route=...)` |
| Palace Electrostatic | `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim.simulation_drc(plan, route=...)` |
| AEDT HFSS Eigenmode | `scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, modeling=...)` |
| AEDT HFSS Driven Terminal or Q3D | No separate call: `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry` and `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` run the same steps before AEDT starts, and refuse there |

`route` is the Palace geometry approximation: `"B"`, the default, keeps the
metal's thickness, and `"A"` makes each film a sheet of zero thickness; pass
`approximation_profile` as you pass it to `set_route`. `modeling` is the AEDT
one, `"thin_film"` or `"solid"`, with no default. A pass on one route or
modeling says nothing about another, and Palace and AEDT never stand for each
other. Only the two Palace classes, on the same plan and route, build the same
model when the plan has no port sheet; with port sheets they differ, because
Eigenmode cuts each sheet to a lumped port.

For a cell meant for several simulations, check the one plan with each:

```python
import scgsim.aedt
import scgsim.palace

plan = pad_plan(gap_um=20.0)
checks = [
    (scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim, {"route": "B"}),
    (scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim, {"route": "B"}),
    (scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim, {"modeling": "solid"}),
]
for simulation, options in checks:
    report = simulation.simulation_drc(plan, **options)
    print(f"{simulation.__module__}.{simulation.__name__}")
    print(report.render_text())
```

A refusal raises, so the loop stops at the first class that refuses the plan.
The Palace checks need `scgsim[palace]`, the AEDT check `scgsim[aedt]`; neither
needs a solver or an AEDT licence.

## What the check takes from the plan {#build-the-plan}

The check takes the `GeometryPlan` itself, before `prepare()`, and uses it as
the simulation will: its Nets, its vacuum region, its Surface-EPR request, its
junctions and port sheets, and its coupon padding. It adds nothing of its own
and leaves the plan as it was. So build the plan once, check it, and give
`plan.prepare()` to the simulation. Something other than a `GeometryPlan`,
such as the component or a snapshot, is refused with the plan to build.

::: {.callout-note title="What a pass means"}
A pass means the model of this plan, on the route or modeling checked, builds
and has no edge or face the meshing stage refuses. It does not promise that
another route, Electrostatic terminals or extra ports will build, and it does
not promise a clean mesh: `mesh()` can still stop with `MeshRepairError` and
name where it stopped. To check one exact set-up, run that simulation's own
`mesh()`.
:::
